title: Follow one MR1 cable
intro: Pick a cable. Match its label at both ends, then compare the named functions. Work deenergized; these routes do not approve energizing or machining.
closedLoop: The encoder returns to its own CL57T drive. The PC receives commanded position, not independent table position; a loose coupler can still escape encoder detection.
axisNote: Four motors, three logical axes. Y-left and Y-right share logical Y; Y-right is not a rotary fourth axis.
labelNote: Source cable IDs come from the corrected cable schedule. Functional-route labels describe additional views and are not new approved harness IDs. Interface labels are planned functions, not proven terminal markings.
viewNote: Published connector numbers and colors are reference clues, not proof of the installed cable or its mating view. Match the actual variant, connector numbering and deenergized continuity before landing a wire.

holds.label: Socket view unverified
holds.reason: The actual v1.1 board socket view, cable attachment and STEP/DIR/GND continuity have not been recorded. The 18-contact socket must be identified by function; GPIO names do not give physical cavity positions. No installed adapter is assumed.

holds.label: Header view unverified
holds.reason: Record the actual STOP or EXP2 mating view, key direction and signal/GND continuity. Do not count cavities from a generic picture.

holds.label: Drive terminals unverified
holds.reason: Confirm all four drive labels say CL57T V4.1. Record the actual P1–P4 terminal face, keying and mating view before inserting contacts.

holds.label: Command interface unfinished
holds.reason: The selected command source is DRIVER0 VCC_IO (+5 V) through a 0.5 A fast branch fuse to +5_MOTION, with DRIVER0 logic GND to CTRL_0V. Its construction and loaded performance remain unqualified. Verify S3=5V, J68 USB-power jumper removed, supply margin, PUL/DIR current and timing, and power-up/down behavior. ENA stays unconnected, so drives stay enabled while STEP/DIR are undefined during MCU reset or the SD bootloader: scope with drive power off. The fuse is overcurrent protection, not voltage protection or isolation. The controller-health/enable interlock remains a separate unfinished requirement.

holds.label: Selected alarm circuit: assembly and tests pending
holds.reason: Four Weidmüller TRP24VDC2COAU 2618530000 relays and one isolated DDR-15G-24 supply are selected in ALARM_INTERFACE.md. Prove ALM conducts healthy and opens on alarm, lost drive power and either wire open. The manufacturer does not identify the polarity parameter. Do not invert firmware to hide a failed test.

holds.label: Module circuit unknown
holds.reason: A TLP281 or HW-399 label does not prove terminals, supplies or isolation. Trace any chosen module, including shared pullups; leaving output VCC floating is not an approved recipe.

holds.label: Return path unverified
holds.reason: Record the controller-side return, control-0V/PE reference and any USB/earthed-PC path. Never remove protective earth to force an open reading.

holds.label: Motor harness untraced
holds.reason: The manufacturer publishes two motor color options. Identify this kit, verify its numbered GX16 view and trace phases while deenergized. Actual phase/encoder pairing, length, fit and shielding remain unrecorded.

holds.label: Encoder harness untraced
holds.reason: The manufacturer publishes six DB15 functions plus a separate shield lead. Verify this matched harness and the actual numbered view while deenergized. The shield has no P2/EGND assignment; no physical or internal-isolation proof is recorded.

holds.label: Motion supply unqualified
holds.reason: The recorded supply is 36 V / 10 A. Four-drive load, regeneration, ripple, branch protection, wire ratings and distribution terminals remain unqualified. No fuse value is selected here.

holds.label: Hardware stop not proved
holds.reason: Protective bonding, independent hardware stopping and gravity-loaded Z support remain unproved. The E-stop design is principles only and is a blocking hold before energizing: spindle-servo mains contactor and/or certified STO, 36 V removal with a Z-drop analysis, coolant in the stop chain and a terminal schedule. ENA is unused; a stopped command stream does not remove torque or prevent movement.

routes.title: X: control cable to CL57T P1

upstream.label: Octopus MOTOR0
upstream.note: STEP/DIR from this empty socket; shared +5_MOTION comes only from DRIVER0 VCC_IO through the 0.5 A fast fuse. No plug-in motor driver. EN remains reserved.

routes.summary: PUL+ and DIR+ share +5_MOTION: DRIVER0 VCC_IO (+5 V) → 0.5 A fast fuse → interface distribution. Separate STEP/DIR MOSFET sinks connect PUL− and DIR− to CTRL_0V when commanded. Selected circuit; not physically accepted.
routes.check: Match the cable label at both ends. Verify PUL and DIR as separate pairs; leave ENA and BRK unconnected.

routes.title: X: socket to interface
routes.summary: These signals come from the empty driver socket. The separate four-pin A1/A2/B1/B2 motor-output plug is unused for this external-drive control cable. The planned interface input names are functional labels until its actual terminals are confirmed. The separate shared command-supply branch uses DRIVER0 VCC_IO through a 0.5 A fast fuse; see Command supply. This branch is not an extra wire in the scheduled CMD-X cable.
routes.check: Identify STEP, DIR and logic return on the actual board. Confirm the cable attachment and interface terminal map before landing conductors. Leave reserved EN and unused socket contacts unconnected.

routes.title: X: drive to motor

connections.reference: Published STEPPERONLINE GX16 pin 1 → A+: Option A white; Option B black. Identify the actual option and numbered connector view; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE GX16 pin 2 → A−: Option A green; Option B green. Identify the actual option and numbered connector view; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE GX16 pin 3 → B+: Option A blue; Option B red. Identify the actual option and numbered connector view; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE GX16 pin 4 → B−: Option A black; Option B blue. Identify the actual option and numbered connector view; not measured.

routes.summary: P3 carries motor phase current. Keep this motor and its encoder paired with the same drive.
routes.check: Identify the actual Option A or B harness; do not mix color schemes. Trace numbered contacts and both coil pairs with all energy isolated and discharged. Never plug or unplug it while powered.

routes.title: X: motor feedback to drive

connections.reference: Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 1, black → P2 EA+. Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 13, blue → P2 EA−. Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 11, yellow → P2 EB+. Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 12, green → P2 EB−. Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 2, red → P2 VCC (drive supply output). Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.
Published STEPPERONLINE DB15 pin 3, white → P2 EGND. Confirm the actual numbered connector view and continuity; not measured.

routes.summary: The drive reads this encoder locally. P2 VCC supplies the encoder; never feed it from an external 5 V or 24 V supply.
routes.check: Trace all six electrical functions and identify the separate shield lead while deenergized. Match the actual numbered DB15 view; route away from motor and bus wiring. Do not add ground bonds.
routes.shieldNote: The seventh, thick black lead is the published shield/drain reference, distinct from the thin black EA+ conductor. It has no P2 or EGND assignment. Keep it individually insulated pending the reviewed shield-bond plan.

routes.title: X: polarized drive power
routes.summary: P4 is polarized DC power. Each drive gets its own protected pair from the distribution point; no drive-to-drive daisy chain.
routes.check: Confirm markings and trace positive to +VDC, negative to GND with all sources isolated. Supply and protection approval remain open.

routes.title: X: ALM and COM− to relay circuit
routes.summary: K-X is Weidmüller 2618530000. Its A1 connects to the fused isolated +23 V alarm bus; ALM switches A2 and COM− returns to ALARM_0V. Both terminals stay off the Octopus GPIO and command ground. See the alarm circuit above for the supply and relay contacts.
routes.check: Assembly remains pending. Prove healthy energizes the relay and alarm, lost drive power, lost alarm supply and either field wire open release it. No guessed polarity setting and no live motor/encoder unplugging.

routes.title: X: separate relay contact → STOP4
routes.summary: New MR1F version 1 firmware reports PG12–PG15 as sampled diagnostics. Older or missing reports remain UNKNOWN. PB1 remains the drive-fault stop; diagnostic samples can miss brief events. Add a 2.2 kΩ pull-up from the input to board 3.3 V and 100 nF from the input to logic GND; LOW only means the contact is closed, not proved machine health.
routes.check: Leave the STOP +5 V contact empty. Relay 21/24 must be isolated from coil A1/A2. Remove DIAG jumper caps. Preserve independent PB1 stopping.

from.label: Four relay NO contacts in series

connections.from: K-YR 14 through other required healthy contacts

routes.summary: PB1 → K-X 11/14 → K-YL 11/14 → K-Z 11/14 → K-YR 11/14 → any other required healthy contacts → logic GND. Add 2.2 kΩ to board 3.3 V and 100 nF to logic GND at PB1. One released relay opens the chain. Welded contacts or a short to GND can defeat this ordinary diagnostic circuit; keep the independent hardware E-stop.
routes.check: Prove every contributor independently using the approved test setup before any coupled dual-Y motion; PB1 is the only drive-fault stop. PB1 is a controller fault input; the independent hardware stop is still required.
routes.otherContributors: Required cabinet/spindle fault sources and their conditioning remain to be established by the reviewed complete circuit.

homeNote: See the home-switch connector references: the reported stock four-wire harness combines Y2 and Z. Our four independent Octopus inputs require verified rewiring; this is not a plug-in stock-harness adapter.
